title: Orchestrator epoch skew triggered rollback-fallback loop during multi-variant rollout
creator: Amina Patel
description: During a staged rollout of a multi-variant model promotion, the orchestrator entered a repeated rollback -> fallback loop across two regions. The loop caused transient mixed-serve, elevated tail latency, and a ~45% increase in token cost for impacted customers for ~32 minutes while autoscaling oscillated. This ticket documents the timeline, root cause analysis, actions taken during the event, and permanent mitigations.
impact_summary: Outage window: ~00:12 UTC to 00:44 UTC on 2026-03-08. Affected: ~12% of production traffic for the deployment (cross-region routes). Symptoms: repeated variant flips, cache churn causing CPU/GPU load spikes, elevated 95/99 p99 latencies, and increased egress costs due to duplicate work. No data loss; no secrets exposed.
timeline:
2026-03-08 00:11 UTC - Canary rollout initiated (2% to variant B)
2026-03-08 00:12 UTC - Orchestrator A (region-1) reports epoch increment and applies new stage mapping
2026-03-08 00:13 UTC - Region-2 does not observe epoch update due to delayed metadata fanout (batching + rate limit). Region-2 controller considers new variant unhealthy and triggers rollback to variant A
2026-03-08 00:14 UTC - Global routing detects mixed serve and applies fallback to fallback-model (costly variant)
2026-03-08 00:15-00:28 UTC - Orchestrator leadership re-election and late metadata fanout cause region-1 to perceive a stale epoch; it reasserts previous stage mapping, flipping variants again. This continues in a loop with approx 30-90s oscillation until 00:44 UTC
2026-03-08 00:44 UTC - Operators manually quiesce rollout, apply fence, and promote a single-source-of-truth config; traffic stabilizes
2026-03-08 01:10 UTC - Post-incident monitoring confirms steady-state and autoscaler damping has recovered
root_cause: Epoch token propagation and application ordering in the orchestrator is not strictly monotonic under metadata fanout delays and batch rate limiting. A leader applied an epoch increment; another region applied a rollback without the epoch, creating divergent perceived desired state. The orchestrator then performed conflicting actions (rollback vs. promote) leading to a flip/flop loop. Secondary causes: missing global rollout semaphore, insufficient circuit breaker for rapid fallback, and KV cache invalidation policy that caused heavy cache eviction during repeated variant warmups.
contributing_factors: 1) Metadata fanout batching and rate limits introduced >30s propagation lag between regions. 2) No strong fencing: epoch increments are applied but not validated against an authoritative source before making promotion/rollback decisions. 3) Autoscaler responded to transient load spikes, amplifying capacity churn. 4) Lack of a cooldown on rollback-triggering health signals.
detection_and_response: We detected the issue via rollback alerting (route-divergence) and increased p99 latency alerts. On-call engaged, reviewed orchestrator logs, and correlated epoch numbers across regional controllers. Response actions included pausing the rollout, applying an authoritative config from the control plane, adding temporary traffic pins to stop promotions, and increasing KV cache TTLs to reduce churn.
mitigation_steps_taken: 1) Manual quiesce of rollout and applied single-source-of-truth config (00:44 UTC). 2) Forced epoch reconciliation across regions and restarted the sidecar in region-2 to flush stale route cache. 3) Temporarily disabled aggressive autoscale policies for the affected pool. 4) Increased metadata fanout budget while we validated fixes.
permanent_actions: Add strict epoch fencing: validate incoming epoch against authoritative control-plane watermark before acting
Introduce rollout global semaphore to serialize promotion/rollback decisions for multi-region deployments
Add cooldown and hysteresis to rollback-triggering health signals to avoid flip-flop on transient failures
Improve metadata fanout: add prioritized fanout for rollout-critical keys + backpressure metrics
Adjust KV cache eviction policy to prefer warm entries for models during rollouts and add an adaptive TTL for cache items created during variant swaps
Add canary-run harness that simulates cross-region propagation delay in CI to catch ordering bugs
Dashboard: surface epoch drift (max - min epoch across controllers) and rollout divergence metric with alert thresholds
Automerge gate: block automated rollouts when epoch drift > threshold or when fanout latency > threshold
verification_plan: 1) Deploy epoch-fencing patch to canary cluster and run synthetic multi-region rollout test (owner: Diego). 2) Run CI rollout harness that injects fanout delays for 48 hours against canary (owner: Priya). 3) Verify dashboard alerts for epoch drift and divergence fire on synthetic tests. 4) After 2 successful synthetic runs without flip/flop, schedule a low-traffic real-world canary with manual oversight. 5) Post-deploy review and sign-off by SRE (Elena).
follow_up_notes: PM and Design notified; no customer-facing incident page required as impact was contained to some high-volume customers—we'll brief affected accounts via CSMs. We will add this incident as a learning example in rollout runbook and run a war-room simulation in next on-call rotation. Estimate for completion of permanent mitigations: 3 sprints (6 weeks).
